ui.update.available: There is a new version of Nayive.
ui.tourSoon: The guided tour is coming soon.
ui.coach.home: Tap the app's name or icon to go back to the home screen.
ui.coach.help: Tap the question mark to see the help.
ui.coach.wait: Take a moment to read it…
ui.fp.loadError: Your folders could not be loaded. Check your connection.
ui.fp.noFolders: You have no folder inside “Files”. Create one with the button below.
ui.install.title: Put Nayive on your home screen
ui.install.lead: It is free, it downloads nothing from a store, and it uninstalls like any app.
ui.install.leadDone: Open it from its icon, like any other app.
ui.install.b1: It sits on your home screen, next to your other apps.
ui.install.b2: It opens without the browser bar: you see more, and better.
ui.install.b3: It starts sooner and several apps keep working with no internet.
ui.install.inapp: You are viewing Nayive inside another app. Open it in Safari or Chrome to install it.
ui.install.unsupported: This browser does not offer to install it. Try Chrome or Edge, or Safari on the iPhone.
ui.install.done: Done. You can now open Nayive from your home screen.
acct.langFailed: The language could not be saved.
acct.tzFailed: The time zone could not be saved.
acct.themeAutoInfo: Turns the theme light at sunrise and dark at sunset, wherever you are. Your location is kept on this device only, rounded to about 10 km. With no location it uses the city your time zone is named after. Changing the theme by hand switches automatic off.
acct.themeAutoGeo: Sunrise and sunset for your location.
acct.themeAutoNoGeo: No location: sunrise and sunset of your time zone.
share.title: Share “{what}”
share.lead: They sign in with their own account and see it in their apps. They can never change it.
share.everyone: You have already shared it with everyone.
share.nobody: There is nobody else on this server.
share.mayadd: They can add files (never delete or change them)
share.leadadd: They sign in with their own account and see it in their apps. They can add files, but never delete or change anything.
share.leadTrip: They sign in with their own account and see the whole trip in their list: stages, documents, notes and photos. They can never change it.
share.people.head: Only following Nayive users
share.link.head: Anyone with the link
share.link.warn: No account needed. They see the photos, your comments, the route so far and where you are (to ~100 m). Never documents or notes.
share.link.none: Link removed. Open Share again to get a new one.
trips.loc.none: Sending your location is not set up
trips.loc.lead: Each trip keeps where you were during its dates, for its Journey map. Two things place you: photos with GPS added to the trip's photo folder, and a location app on your phone, in the background. You can switch it off in a trip's edit dialog.
trips.loc.overlandHow: Tap “Set up Overland”: the app takes this address by itself. Then open it and switch tracking on. It works for all your trips.
trips.loc.gpsloggerHow: Tap “Set up GPSLogger”: the app takes all its settings from here. Then open it once and let it start. It works for all your trips.
trips.loc.onPhone: Open this page on your phone to set the app up there.
trips.loc.stopBody: The address stops working. The app on your phone keeps sending to it and will fail every time, so turn it off there too. The places already saved stay.
trips.loc.info:
Overland (iPhone) and GPSLogger (Android) are free, open-source phone apps that send your location in the background. Neither is ours.
Nothing to install on your VPS: Nayive already receives it. Just install the app on your phone.
More: https://overland.p3k.app and https://gpslogger.app
trips.track: Save where I am during this trip
trips.trackInfo: Photos with GPS and a location app place you on this trip's Journey map. Nothing is saved outside its dates. Positions are rounded to about 100 m.
trips.mapJourney: Journey: where you went and your photos
trips.journeyEmpty: Nothing yet: this trip has no locations or photos with a place.
trips.journeyCaption: Route so far, photos and where you are (to ~100 m): what the public link shows.
trips.introMyLocation: Your location for the trips' Journey maps: set up Overland (iPhone) or GPSLogger (Android).
habits.gridHint: Full dot: done. Empty: it was due and was not done. Tap a habit to see its longest streak and this month's percentage.
habits.name: Name
habits.noData: No data yet: check your connection
habits.noHabitsHint: Drink water, walk, read… Create the first one with (+) and tick it every day you keep it.
habits.noMonth: Nothing to show in this month
split.addEntry: Record an expense or a payment
split.currencyLocked: Once there are expenses the currency can no longer be changed.
split.deleteGroupBody: “{name}” and all its expenses will go to the bin.
split.needTwo: Choose who pays and who is paid
split.noEntriesHint: Record the first one with (+). Every expense says who paid and who it was for.
split.noGroupsHint: A trip, the flat, a dinner… Create a group with (+) and note who pays what.
split.others: The other people, one per line
split.pctSum: They add up to {n} % and must be 100 %
split.peopleLead: Mark which one is you. Someone with recorded expenses cannot be removed, only hidden.
ui.room.title: Not enough space
ui.room.trashBody:
The bin is holding {held}. Emptying it would leave plenty of room.

Everything in it will be deleted for good.
ui.room.emptyFail: The bin could not be emptied.
ui.quota.title: Your space is almost full
ui.quota.bin: Bin: empty it in Drive. Deleted files still take space until then.
ui.quota.binHolds: Bin: it holds {held}. Empty it in Drive: deleted files still take space until then.
ui.quota.chat: Chat: the photos and files in your chats take space too. Delete the chats you no longer need, or turn on auto-delete.
ui.quota.big: Big files: videos are usually the biggest. Delete the ones you no longer need.
ui.needJs: This page needs JavaScript enabled to work.
login.blankIfNew: Leave blank if you are new
launcher.introLead: 12 apps, your data stays yours and everything works offline. Tap an app to open it. The calendar and the tasks live inside Planner.
launcher.introGear: Opens and closes the settings row.
launcher.introAccount: Change your password, the reminders, the bin periods, the event colour and the colour schemes.
launcher.introInstall: Install Nayive on your phone or computer, with its own icon.
launcher.introTip: Tip: inside an app, tap its name or its icon (top left) to come back here.
scm.info:
You can change the four background tones, from the darkest to the lightest, and the accent colour. The text and the links do not change, and the text on accent buttons is picked for you.

The active scheme of each mode applies to every app in your cloud.
scm.accentLow: The accent colour is hard to see on these tones ({ratio} : 1). Aim for 3 : 1 or more.
scm.needOne: At least one {kind} scheme must remain.
scm.assignHead: Which scheme applies to each mode
acct.mustSet: Your account has no password yet. Create one to continue.
acct.tooShort: The password must be at least 4 characters long.
acct.changeFailed: The password could not be changed.
acct.autoDeleteMsg: They will be deleted after {n} days
acct.notifsInfo: Nayive warns you shortly before each calendar event, even with the app closed. Turn it on for every device where you want the alerts.
acct.notifsOn: Notifications are on for this device
acct.notifsAsk: Nayive is installed. Turn the notifications on here so your phone reminds you of your events.
acct.notifsBlocked: Your browser is blocking notifications. Turn them on in the browser settings.
acct.notifsUnsupported: This browser does not support notifications.
acct.notifsIos: On iPhone and iPad you must install Nayive on the Home Screen to receive notifications.
acct.notifsStale: Notifications got disconnected. Turn them on again.
acct.pushOffBody:
Notifications are not on for this device, so you will not get reminders or messages.
Turn them on in My account?
push.tripBody: Get ready for the trip to {dest} (leaves on {date}).
push.locationOnBody: Trip to {dest}: turn on the location app on your phone.
push.locationOffTitle: You can turn off your location
push.locationOffBody: Your trip to {dest} is over: you can turn off the location app on your phone.
push.convertFailedBody: “{name}” could not be converted. The original is still in place.
planner.introLead: Calendar, Tasks and Habits on one screen. Drag the bars between them to give one more room than the other.
planner.introLeadPhone: Calendar, Tasks and Habits on one screen. Below you see one at a time: pick which with the three buttons above.
planner.introRestore: If you folded Habits away (with the arrow in its header), this little bar at the bottom opens it again.
planner.introHelp: Every pane has its own “?” button with that app's help. This one is Planner's.
planner.introSync: One single plug for all three panes, always showing the worst: plugged in and green, everything uploaded; blue, in progress; unplugged and amber, offline (your changes are safe); red, something is wrong. Tap it and all three read from the server again.
planner.introTip: Tip: tap the name or the “Planner” icon to go back to the list of apps.
ui.quotaExceeded: The disk quota has been exceeded.
st.whichAlbumNote: Choose the folder in your Files where these photos should go.
st.pickAlbumToast: Choose the album to save the photos in.
st.keptToRetry: They are still here: press Upload to try again.
ui.sync.offline: Offline — your changes will be saved when you reconnect
ui.sync.needsAuth: Session expired — sign in again to upload your changes
ui.sync.error: Could not save — check your connection
ui.sync.conflict: Changed on another device — your changes are only on this one
ui.store.notRead: The file could not be read: nothing is saved until it can be.
ui.store.loading: The file is still being read: try again in a moment.
ui.store.badFile: This file holds something I do not understand: it opens read-only, so it is not damaged.
ui.settingsNotRead: Your settings could not be read: they are not saved until they can be.
tasks.addPh: Describe a task to add it…
tasks.introLead: Your list of things to do. A task can have sub-tasks, and ticking it off moves it to the “Done” list.
tasks.introAdd: Adds the task written in the field next to it.
tasks.introOpen: Opens the field to write a new task.
tasks.introAddSub: The (+) icon on each task adds a sub-task to it too.
tasks.introDrag: Drag a sub-task's dotted grip to change its order or move it to another task.
tasks.introUndone: In the “Done” list, this button puts the task back into “Active”.
tasks.introSync: The plug shows how saving is going: plugged in and green, everything uploaded; blue, in progress; unplugged and amber, offline (your changes are safe); red, something is wrong. Tap it to load the list from the server again.
tasks.birthdayOne: Wish {name} a happy birthday — turns {n} today
tasks.tripReminder: Get ready for the trip to {dest} (leaves on {date})
tasks.emptyNoneBody: Add your first task above to get started.
tasks.emptyActiveBody: Add new tasks with the + button
tasks.dragHandle: Drag to move to another task
tasks.planDaysLabel: How long it takes (leave it empty if you don't know yet)
tasks.planAfterHint: It starts once every ticked one is done. Only sub-tasks of this same task.
tasks.planNoSiblings: This task has no other sub-tasks.
tasks.planTotalTitle: How long the whole task takes; work that runs in parallel counts once
tasks.planSlack: How much it can slip without moving the end
tasks.planAskOne: “{name}” is not done yet. Mark it too?
tasks.planAskMany: {n} sub-tasks before this one are not done. Mark them too?
tasks.introPlan: On each sub-task it opens how many days it takes and which ones it waits for. The lines on the left say what waits for what: a filled dot can be done now, a hollow one is waiting, a grey one is done.
split.searchPh: Search by description, person or amount…
split.perCurrencyTip: Not converted: each currency on its own
split.copyTip: Copies the balances as text so you can send them on WhatsApp or Telegram
split.introLead: Expenses shared with friends, in any currency. Every group says at all times who owes how much to whom.
split.introGroupLead: One group up close: its expenses, its payments, and who owes how much to whom.
split.introAddGroup: Creates a group: the name, the currency its accounts are kept in, and who is in it (you and the others, one name per line).
split.introOpenGroup: Tap the row. On the right you see your balance in that group: green is what you are owed, red what you owe.
split.introArchive: On the right of every group of yours. Puts a settled group away: it leaves the list and moves to “Archived”.
split.introArchived: At the foot of the list, with the number of groups put away. Tap it to show them or hide them again.
split.introShared: Groups another Nayive user has let you see. Read only: you can look and copy the summary, but not record or change anything.
split.introAddEntry: An expense (amount, currency, who paid, who it is for and how it is split) or a payment from one person to another.
split.introTabs: “Expenses” is everything recorded, newest first. “Balances” says how much each person is up or down, and who pays whom to settle.
split.introSearch: Appears from six expenses on. Searches by concept, person, date or amount.
split.introEditEntry: Tap any expense or payment in the list to open it again and change it.
split.introDelEntry: Inside the expense's own card. It goes at once, with six seconds to undo it from the notice at the bottom.
split.introModes: Equally, by amounts, by shares or by %. The cents always add up to the total.
split.introFx: Every expense can be in its own currency: type that day's rate and the list shows the ≈ in the group's currency. The last rate for each currency is remembered.
split.introPerCur: In “Balances”, only when there are expenses in two or more currencies. Shows one block per currency, converting nothing.
split.introBack: Goes back to the group list.
split.introPay: In “Balances”, every “who pays whom” line has this button: it records that payment with the amount already filled in.
split.introPeople: Who is in the group: add people, rename them, and mark which one is you. Anyone who already has expenses cannot be removed, only hidden.
split.introDelete: Only on a group already archived. It asks first, then sends the group and all its expenses to the bin.
split.introCopy: The balances as plain text, ready to paste into WhatsApp, Telegram or an email. The same button sits at the foot of “Balances”.
split.introCsv: Every expense in a CSV file, to open in Calc and do your own sums.
split.introEdit: The group's name, and the currency its accounts are kept in. Once there are expenses the currency is fixed.
split.introShare: Another Nayive user can see the group (read only). With “Copy summary” you send the balances on WhatsApp or Telegram to anyone who is not.
split.introSync: The plug shows how saving is going: plugged in and green, everything uploaded; blue, in progress; unplugged and amber, offline (your changes are safe); red, something is wrong. Tap it to read the groups from the server again.
habits.targetInfo: Left blank, the habit is a yes or no. With a number (3 glasses of water), each tap adds one and the day counts as done when you reach it.
habits.introLead: Your everyday routines. Tick the ones you keep and see how many days in a row you are on.
habits.introAdd: Create a habit: name, icon, colour, the days it is due and, if you want, a daily target (3 glasses of water).
habits.introMark: The round button on each habit marks it done today; another tap undoes it. With a target, each tap adds one.
habits.introYesterday: If it was due yesterday and you did not tick it, the row says so. Tap it and it counts as done.
habits.introEdit: Tap a habit's name to change it, see its best streak and this month's percentage, archive it or bring it back.
habits.introMonth: The “Month” tab is the month grid: a full dot for every day kept and a gap for every day it was due and was not.
habits.introCollapse: Folds Habits away inside Planner to give Tasks all the room. A little bar with an up arrow stays at the bottom to open it again.
habits.introSync: The plug shows how saving is going: plugged in and green, everything uploaded; blue, in progress; unplugged and amber, offline (your changes are safe); red, something is wrong. Tap it to read the habits from the server again.
ui.draftNote: Only on this device until you save it
ui.conflictBody:
“{name}” was saved from another device after you opened it. Your changes did NOT replace it: they are still on this device.

Save your version as a copy?
ui.conflictCopy: Save my version as a copy
ui.fileGone: The file no longer exists on the server.
ui.saveAsExists: “{name}” already exists in that folder. Replace it with this document?
ui.prefsUnread: Your saved settings could not be read: they are left alone until they can be.
ui.openFailed: The file could not be opened.
ui.notUploaded: Not uploaded — your changes are safe on this device
ui.saveFailedConn: Could not save — sign in again or check your connection
text.introLead: A text and code editor (html, css, js, json, txt and more). Files open from Drive and save themselves as you type.
text.introImport: Uploads a file from this device and opens it.
text.introOpen: Opens a text file saved in your Drive.
text.introSaveAs: Saves the content as a new file.
text.introLang: Language for the syntax colouring (by default, from the extension).
text.introWrap: Breaks long lines so they fit the screen.
text.introMargin: Column where the right-margin guide line is drawn.
text.noTextFiles: This folder holds no text files.
text.badExt: Text does not save “.{ext}” files. Choose another extension.
text.introMdView: Markdown only: switches between the document as it reads and the text to write it.
text.emptyDoc: Empty document — type or import a file.
text.notYours: It belongs to somebody else: save it as a copy of your own.
text.importFailed: The file could not be imported.
text.notText: “{name}” is not a text file: Text does not open it.
text.notUtf8: “{name}” is not UTF-8: it opens read-only, so it is not damaged. “Save as” makes a UTF-8 copy.
text.renameFailed: The file could not be renamed.
text.statNote: The whole document, as it stands right now.
text.mdImgOff: Image not shown: only images beside this file are loaded
write.introLead: A word processor that saves to .docx with no conversion. The document saves itself as you type.
write.introFormatBar: On the phone: shows or hides the formatting bar. It folds away as soon as you touch the text.
write.introMoreBar: On the phone: opens the rest of the bar (font, tables, indents, zoom, find…).
write.introFileMenu: On the phone: open, import, save as, page, header and settings live here.
write.introNew: Start a blank document without leaving the app.
write.introOpen: Opens another document from your Drive.
write.introImport: Uploads a .docx from this device and opens it.
write.introSaveAs: Saves the document as a new copy.
write.introHeader: Edit the header and the footer.
write.introSettings: Settings: document mode, proofing language and correcting as you type.
write.editorSlow: The editor took too long to load. Reload the page if it does not appear.
write.openDocFailed: The document could not be opened
write.waitForDoc: Wait for the document to load
write.headerFailed: The header could not be opened
write.cursorInTable: Put the cursor inside a table
write.selectCells: Select several cells for inside borders
write.pageSetupFailed: The setup could not be applied
write.formatUnsupported: That format cannot be opened yet
write.offlineSafe: Offline — your changes are safe on this device
write.newDropsDraft: The current draft is unsaved and will be lost.
write.pdfHint: In the print dialog, choose "Save as PDF" as the destination.
write.introPrint: Print the document, or save it as a PDF from the same dialog.
write.statNote: The body of the document only: headers, footers and notes are not counted.
write.introStats: Words, characters and pages in the document.
write.introPageNum: Numbers the pages by itself. Use it inside the header or the footer.
write.paTouchNote: Only what you change here is applied; the rest of the paragraph stays as it is. Set the tab stop to 0 to clear them all.
write.introPara: Paragraph spacing, indents, lists and tab stops.
write.paListNote: Changing the list style clears the Undo history.
write.notInList: The cursor is not in a list
write.pickTemplatesNote: Any .docx in this folder becomes a template.
write.restoreBody: The copy saved before this session ({size}) will be opened. What is here now becomes the copy, so you can undo it.
write.noBackupYet: There is no previous copy of this document yet
write.introTemplates: Start from a template: any .docx in the folder you choose.
write.introRestore: Go back to the copy saved before this session.
lock.title: Password
lock.setBody: The document will be saved encrypted. If you forget the password nobody can open it: there is no way to recover it.
lock.noMatch: The two passwords are not the same.
lock.offBody: The document will be saved unencrypted again.
lock.noCrypto: This browser cannot encrypt here: a secure connection is needed.
lock.draftBody: This draft is encrypted and exists only on this device. Without the password there is no way to open it.
lock.pastTitle: It has already been saved without a password
lock.pastBody:
“{name}” is already saved unencrypted, on this device and on the server. A password now does NOT erase those copies.

Clean copy: Nayive saves the protected document under another name and deletes this one for good, out of the Bin too. Even then, the nightly backup keeps the old file for about 30 days.
lock.pastDraftBody:
What you have written is already saved unencrypted on this device, in the automatic draft. The password protects what comes next, but it does not erase that.

To leave nothing behind, start a new document, put the password on before typing, and copy the text there.
lock.wiped: The old file has been deleted for good
lock.wipeFailed: The old file could not be deleted
write.introLock: Put a password on the document: it is saved encrypted and opens only with it.
write.dictSaveFailed: Your dictionary could not be saved
write.dictUnread: Your dictionary could not be read: “{word}” was not added.
write.autocorrectNote: Turns straight quotes into typographic ones, "..." into "…" and "--" into "—". Off by default: it gets in the way of file names and code.
write.chromeNote: The toolbar puts everything in one row of icons; the pull-down menus spread it over File, Edit, View… as in Word. They do the same things.
ui.clipboardBlocked: The browser will not let the menu use the clipboard. Use Ctrl+X, Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V.
calendar.introLead: Your calendar in a single .ics file. Click a day to create an event and drag it to change its time or its day.
calendar.introLeadPhone: Your calendar in a single .ics file. In the month, tap a day to see its events below and + to add one.
calendar.introWeek: Seven-day view with today in the middle: the 3 days before and the 3 after.
calendar.introGoTo: Jumps to a given day, month and year — or back to today.
calendar.introViews: On the phone: the views (Day, Month, Agenda).
calendar.introAdd: Creates an event on the marked day of the month view.
calendar.introSync: The plug shows how saving is going: plugged in and green, everything uploaded; blue, in progress; unplugged and amber, offline (your changes are safe); red, something is wrong. Tap it to read the calendar from the server again.
calendar.title: Title
calendar.tzHintFloating: The time follows the time zone of whatever device you look at it on.
calendar.tzHintPinned: The time stays fixed in the chosen place, wherever you are when you look at it.
calendar.tzHelpLead: Every timed event can be set up in two ways, in the field
calendar.tzPinnedHelp: — The time stays fixed in the chosen place. A flight leaving at 14:30 in Tokyo still shows 14:30 if you look at it from Tokyo, and is converted automatically (to 07:30, say) if you look at it from Madrid.
calendar.tzFloatingHelp: — The time follows your current time zone, the device's at any moment. Handy for personal routines (a medicine at 8:00, say) that must happen at that hour wherever you are.
calendar.tzInCalHelp: when a pinned event's zone does not match yours, you will see a small tag next to the time (“GMT+9”, say) telling you which time zone it belongs to.
calendar.badTz: “{tz}” is not a recognised time zone
calendar.editsSeries: Editing a repeating event edits the whole series.
calendar.introSettings: Settings: sync this calendar with your phones, and export events.
calendar.set.syncLead: Your phones read and change these events directly. Nayive keeps the master copy.
calendar.set.syncInfo:
It uses CalDAV, the standard way to sync calendars. The iPhone has it built in. Android needs DAVx⁵, a free, open-source app (not ours).
Each phone gets its own password, never your Nayive one.
More: https://www.davx5.com
calendar.set.iphoneHow: Tap “Set up iPhone”, then open Settings › General › VPN & Device Management and install the Nayive profile. Your events appear in the Calendar app.
calendar.set.androidHow: Install DAVx⁵, then tap “Set up DAVx⁵”: it takes the address and password from here. Your events appear in the phone's Calendar app.
calendar.needDates: Set the start and end dates
calendar.nothingToExport: There are no events between those dates
calendar.pdfHint: In the print dialog, choose "Save as PDF" as the destination.
contact.introLead: Your address book in a single .vcf file you can take to your phone. Search the bar by name, email or phone (digits only).
contact.introSettings: Settings: sync these contacts with your phones, and import or export .vcf files.
contact.introDedup: Finds repeated contacts and helps you merge them.
contact.introSelect: Ticks several contacts in the list so you can merge them by hand — for the repeats the scanner cannot see. You can also open it by holding a contact down.
contact.set.syncLead: Your phones read and change these contacts directly. Nayive keeps the master copy.
contact.set.syncInfo:
It uses CardDAV, the standard way to sync contacts. The iPhone has it built in. Android needs DAVx⁵, a free, open-source app (not ours).
Each phone gets its own password, never your Nayive one.
More: https://www.davx5.com
contact.set.iphoneHow: Tap “Set up iPhone”, then open Settings › General › VPN & Device Management and install the Nayive profile. Your contacts appear in the Contacts app.
contact.set.androidHow: Install DAVx⁵, then tap “Set up DAVx⁵”: it takes the address and password from here. Your contacts appear in the phone's Contacts app.
dav.onPhone: Open this page on your phone to set it up there, or type the values below.
contact.set.exportRow: Download all contacts as a .vcf file
contact.introSync: The plug shows how saving is going: plugged in and green, everything uploaded; blue, in progress; unplugged and amber, offline (your changes are safe); red, something is wrong. Tap it to load the address book from the server again.
contact.emptyBody: Press + to create one, or import a .vcf file from your phone.
contact.needSomething: Add at least a name, organisation, phone or email
contact.removeFromGroup: Remove from the group — not the same contact
contact.groupClean: That group has no duplicates left
contact.nothingToExport: There are no contacts to export
contact.readFailed: The file could not be read
contact.noVcards: The file holds no vCard contacts
media.noAccess: You no longer have access to this folder.
music.introLead: Listen to the audio in a folder of your Drive and its subfolders. Tap a song to queue it.
music.introFolder: Shows the current folder; tap it to change it.
music.introSearch: Search your library by title, album or artist.
music.introRescan: Scan the folder again in case it changed.
music.introGroup: These four buttons group by songs, albums, artists or folders.
music.introOrder: Plays the queue in order or at random.
music.introLoadList: Loads a saved playlist into the queue.
music.introSaveList: Saves the current queue as a playlist.
music.saveQueue: Save the queue as a playlist
music.needFolder: Music needs a folder with your music in it. Reload the page to pick it again.
music.whereFolderNote: Choose the folder where you keep your music. You can change it later by tapping its name.
music.pickSong: Choose a song from your library
music.pickAlbum: Choose an album to see its songs.
music.pickArtist: Choose an artist to see their songs.
music.pickFolder: Choose a folder to see the songs it holds.
music.queueEmpty: The queue is empty. Add songs from the library, by dragging them here or with the + button.
music.saveHint: The current queue ({n} songs) will be saved under the name you give it.
music.needListName: Type a name for the playlist.
music.listSaveFailed: The playlist could not be saved.
music.noLists: You have not saved any playlist yet.
music.listUpdateFailed: The saved playlist could not be updated.
movies.introLead: Watch the videos in a folder of your Drive. Tap a film to play it.
movies.introFolder: Shows the current folder; tap it to change it.
movies.introRescan: Scan the folder again in case it changed.
movies.introGroup: These three buttons group by films, genres or folders.
movies.introPosters: Downloads the missing posters from TMDB.

calc.introLead: A spreadsheet with formulas (opens and saves xlsx and csv). Start a cell with = to write a formula; the sheet saves itself.

calc.introFileMenu: On the phone: import, open and save as live here.
calc.introMoreBar: On the phone: opens the rest of the bar (font, alignment, rows and columns, merge, freeze…).
calc.introImport: Uploads a sheet from this device and opens it.
calc.introOpen: Opens a sheet saved in your Drive.
calc.introSaveAs: Saves the sheet as a new file.
calc.introFx: Inserts a function, with help to choose it.
calc.introRowsCols: The next four buttons insert or delete rows and columns.
calc.introAlign: Horizontal and vertical alignment, and wrapping the text inside the cell.
calc.introSort: Sorts the rows by the selected column, smallest first or the other way round.
calc.introFreeze: Keeps the first columns or rows in place as you scroll.
calc.introFormat: The bar formats the selection: font, bold, colour, borders, alignment, merge, number format and freezing columns.

drive.introLead: Your files on the server. Drag the edge between the panes to see two folders at once; the action buttons switch on when you select something.
drive.introSearch: Search by name across the whole drive (* and ? work).
drive.introUpload: Uploads files or folders (or drag them onto the window).
drive.introDownload: Downloads the folder or whatever you have selected.
drive.introMore: On the phone: sharing and the bin live here.
drive.introMove: Moves what is selected to another folder.
drive.introCopy: Copies what is selected to another folder.
drive.introLink: Copies a direct link to the file.
drive.introShare: Shares what is selected with other people.
drive.introTrash: Sends what is selected to the bin.
drive.introBigFiles: Opens/Closes the list of your biggest files, to free space.
drive.introSync: The plug shows how the connection is: plugged in and green, all well; blue, an operation is under way; unplugged and red, something is wrong. Tap it to read the folder from the server again.
drive.trashHolds: The bin is holding {held} (tap to empty it)
drive.diskFullBody:
The disk is nearly full and the bin is holding {held}.

Emptying it frees that space, but everything inside will be deleted for good.
drive.bigNote: Deleted files go to the bin: the space comes back only when the bin is emptied.
drive.searchTip: Search by name across the whole drive. Wildcards work: * (several characters) and ? (one)
drive.sbNote: (capital and small letters count the same)
drive.sbNoFilters: No filters: all of Drive shows.
drive.introSearchBuilder: Advanced search: by name, type and date changed, with a live count.

trips.introLead: Plan trips. Open a trip to add stages to it, see the route on the map (each leg by its transport) and attach tickets and bookings.
trips.introExport: Prints the whole trip, or saves it as a PDF from the same dialog.
trips.introShare: Another Nayive user can see the trip (read only). The same dialog shows who has it and lets you take it back.
trips.introSync: The plug shows how saving is going: plugged in and green, everything uploaded; blue, in progress; unplugged and amber, offline (your changes are safe); red, something is wrong. Tap it to read your trips from the server again.
trips.introStage: A stage is each stop of the trip: the place, when you arrive and leave, and what you carry on with to the next one. The map draws a dot per stage and a line between them.
trips.introDiscover: Tick what interests you about that city — museums, exhibitions, concerts, shopping… — and the search opens in the device's own browser. Nayive looks nothing up: it only writes the question.
trips.introEditStage: Place, dates and times, outbound transport, lodging, notes and documents. Tapping anywhere on the card opens it too.
trips.introToggleStage: The eye switches a stage off without deleting it: it folds down to the title alone and leaves the map. Handy for plans that are not certain yet.
trips.introDeleteStage: Deletes the stage from the trip. Undo, at the bottom, puts it back.
trips.introDrag: Drag a stage's dotted grip to change its order. The map route follows the order of the list.
trips.introMap: The colour of each leg on the map is the transport you leave that stage with (the key is above the map). Hovering over a stage card draws its leg as a solid line on the map.
trips.toggleStage: Switch the stage on or off
trips.docsInfo:
Every document can be a link or a copy.

“Link” points at a file already in your Files: if you change it there later, the trip always shows the current version and it takes no extra space.

“Upload” saves a copy inside this trip's folder: it stays fixed even if you change the original.
trips.endBeforeStart: The end date cannot be earlier than the start date.
trips.endBeforeStartTime: The end date/time cannot be earlier than the start.
trips.filesNeedNet: Attaching or removing files needs a connection. Text changes do save offline.

trips.createFailed: The trip could not be created — try again.

trips.docLinked: Linked to a file in your drive

trips.shareTrip: Share this trip with other people

trips.typeLocationForTz: Type a location above to detect its time zone.
trips.linkExisting: Link a file that is already in your Files
trips.loadFilesFailed: Your files could not be loaded — check your connection.
trips.noFilesInDrive: There are no files in your “Files” folder.

Each item is deleted for good once it has spent this many days in the bin. The countdown starts for each item when you sent it here, not from now.

photos.editHint: Tap a photo to edit and comment on it. When you close the editor, the photo shows the changes.
photos.placesInfo:
Place names are asked of OpenStreetMap (the Nominatim service) from the GPS coordinates of your photos. Only those coordinates are sent, never the photos.

Each name is stored in data/photos/places.json so it is never asked for twice.

games.introLead: Small games that work with no connection. Pick one below.
games.introBack: Note: press the name of the game to go back to all the games.
games.introSudoku: Fill the grid with the numbers 1 to 9, none of them repeated in the same row, column or box. The pencil jots down a square's candidates while you think it over.
games.intro2048: Slide the tiles: two the same merge into one twice as big. The goal is to reach 2048.
games.introMines: Uncover every square with no mine. Each number says how many mines touch it; press it once they are all flagged and the rest open at once.
games.introInvaders: Move the ship and shoot the rows of aliens before they come down to you.
games.introAsteroids: Turn the ship, thrust and break the rocks: each one splits into smaller ones.
games.introSync: The plug shows how saving is going: plugged in and green, everything uploaded; blue, in progress; unplugged and amber, offline (your changes are safe); red, something is wrong. Tap it to read the records from the server again.
games.hint2048: Use the arrow keys, or swipe.
games.minesLost: Boom! You stepped on a mine.
games.hintMines: Tap to uncover. Long-press, or right-click, to plant a flag.
games.hintSudoku: Tap a square and pick the number below. The pencil writes small notes.
games.introSound: Turns the game sounds on or off. The choice is kept on this device.
games.hintInvaders: Move with the arrows and fire with the space bar. On a phone, drag and tap.
games.hintAsteroids: Turn and thrust with the arrow keys, fire with the space bar - or use the keys below.
games.introTetris: Fit the falling pieces into full rows: a complete row clears and everything above it comes down.
games.hintTetris: Arrows to move and rotate, space to drop - or use the keys below.
games.introChess: Play against the machine: tap a piece and then the square to move it to. The three bars say how hard it thinks.
games.hintChess: Tap a piece, then the square to move it to.
games.chessNoMate: No pieces left to mate with: a draw.
games.chessFifty: Fifty moves with no pawn moved and nothing taken: a draw.
games.chessRepeat: The same position three times: a draw.
games.introSolitaire: The Klondike patience: fill the four piles at the top, each from the ace up. Tap a card and then where it goes; tap it twice to send it home.
games.hintSolitaire: Tap a card, then where it goes. Tap it twice to send it home.
games.introCheckers: Play against the machine: tap a piece and then the square to move it to. Taking is compulsory, and the red squares say which pieces have to.
games.hintCheckers: Tap a piece, then the square to move it to.
games.checkersYouWin: It has no move left: you win.
games.checkersYouLose: You have no move left: the machine wins.
games.checkersDrawMoves: Forty moves with nothing taken and no man moved: a draw.
games.checkersRepeat: The same position three times: a draw.

mail.err.hosts: Type the servers of this provider.
mail.err.offline: No connection. Try again when you are online.
mail.err.down: The mail server does not answer. Try again later.
mail.missingTray: This account has no such tray.
mail.removed: Account removed. Its mail stays on its server; its Nayive labels were deleted.
mail.introLead: Read the mail of your accounts (Gmail and others) here.
mail.introTrays: Inbox, Drafts, Sent, Spam and Trash. The number is the mail you have not read.
mail.introRead: Tap a message to read it. Opening it marks it as read.
mail.introSearch: Searches the open tray: senders, subjects and text. Press Enter to search.
mail.introSync: Green: the mail server answered. Tap it to check for new mail.
mail.nameHint: Shown to the people who get your mail.
mail.err.blocked: This provider does not let other apps in with a password.
mail.prov.gmail.what: Gmail needs an app password: a special password, just for Nayive. Your normal Google password does not work here.
mail.prov.gmail.steps:
Turn on 2-Step Verification in your Google account (Google requires it).
Open the page below, type a name (for example Nayive) and press Create.
Copy the 16 letters it shows and paste them here. Spaces do not matter.
mail.prov.microsoft.what: Microsoft no longer lets other apps in with a password (since September 2024). It only allows its own sign-in, which Nayive cannot do yet.
mail.prov.microsoft.steps:
You can keep reading this mail at outlook.com.
Or forward it to a Gmail account and add that one here.
mail.prov.yahoo.what: Yahoo needs an app password. Your normal Yahoo password does not work here.
mail.prov.yahoo.steps:
Open the page below (Account security).
Choose “Generate app password”, type Nayive and press Generate.
Copy the password and paste it here.
mail.prov.icloud.what: iCloud needs an app-specific password. Your Apple Account password does not work here.
mail.prov.icloud.steps:
Two-factor authentication must be on in your Apple Account.
Open the page below: Sign-In and Security › App-Specific Passwords, and create one called Nayive.
Copy it and paste it here.
mail.prov.aol.what: AOL needs an app password. Your normal AOL password does not work here.
mail.prov.aol.steps:
Open the page below (Account security).
Choose “Generate app password”, pick “Other app” and type Nayive.
Copy the password and paste it here.
mail.prov.gmx.what: GMX uses your normal GMX password.
mail.prov.gmx.steps:
In GMX, open Settings › POP3 & IMAP and allow access (it is off at first).
Type your normal GMX password here.
mail.prov.fastmail.steps:
Open the page below (Privacy & Security › App passwords).
Create a new one with access to “Mail (IMAP/POP/SMTP)”.
Copy it and paste it here.
mail.prov.proton.what: Proton Mail only lets apps in through its Bridge program on a computer, so Nayive cannot read it.
mail.prov.proton.steps:
You can keep reading it at proton.me.
Or forward it to another account and add that one here.
mail.prov.other.what: Any provider that allows IMAP. Type its two servers: its help pages list them (search for “IMAP settings”).
mail.prov.other.steps:
Google Workspace on your own domain? Choose Gmail instead.
Many providers want an app password, not your normal one: look in their security settings.
mail.emptyTrashAsk: Delete everything in the Trash for good?
mail.introDelete: Moves the messages to the Trash. You can undo it, or restore them from the Trash later.
mail.introLabels: Put your own labels on messages (several each). Tap a label on the left to see its messages, from every account.
mail.introSelect: Pick several messages to act on them all at once. A long press or a right click on a row also starts it.
mail.introSettings: Your mail accounts (add, remove) and how many days mail stays in the Trash.
mail.labelDup: A label with that name already exists.
mail.noLabels: No labels yet. Make one here.
mail.trashBar: Mail in the Trash is deleted for good after {n} days.
mail.trashDaysHint: Gmail empties its own Trash after 30 days, whatever this says.
mail.err.notray: This account has no such tray.
mail.introLabelAdd: Make a new label: its name and colour. A label's pencil (or a long press on it) edits or deletes it.
mail.labelNeedName: Type a name for the label.
mail.err.norcpt: Type whom to send it to.
mail.err.addr: An address is not valid. Check the To, Cc and Bcc fields.
mail.introCompose: Write a new message. It is saved in Drafts as you type.
mail.introReply: Reply to the sender, to everyone, or forward the message (with its files).
mail.subject: Subject
mail.err.url: That JMAP server address is not valid (it must be https).
mail.jmapUrlHint: Its address, as its help pages give it: mail.example.com or a full https URL.
mail.prov.fastmailjmap.what: Fastmail over JMAP, its own modern way: faster than IMAP. It needs an API token, not your password.
mail.prov.fastmailjmap.steps:
Open the page below: Settings › Privacy & Security › Manage API tokens.
Create a new token of type JMAP with access to Email and Email submission.
Copy it (Fastmail shows it only once) and paste it here.
mail.prov.jmap.what: Any server that speaks JMAP (Stalwart, Cyrus, Apache James…). Type its address and your password or API token.
mail.prov.jmap.steps:
Nayive finds the rest by itself (.well-known/jmap).
The server must allow sending too, or mail can be read but not sent.
mail.spamBar: Mail that looks like junk. You can delete it all for good.
mail.emptySpamAsk: Delete everything in Spam for good?
mail.err.toobig: The message is too big for your mail server.
mail.err.private: That server is on a private network: Nayive does not connect to it.
mail.err.key: Type this account's password again (Settings › its key button).
mail.err.smtp: Mail can be read but not sent: check the SMTP (outgoing) server, its port and the password.
mail.notSaved: The draft could not be saved. The message is still here.
mail.cut: This message is very long: only its beginning is shown.
mail.showImagesAlways: Always show pictures from the internet
mail.showImagesAlwaysHint: Then the sender can tell when you open their messages.
mail.failedN: {n} could not be changed: the server refused them.
mail.notSent: Not sent; it is in Drafts.
bookmarks.cycle: A folder cannot go inside itself.
bookmarks.title: Title
bookmarks.deleteCounts: Folders: {folders} · Bookmarks: {bookmarks}. All of them are deleted.
bookmarks.emptyAll: No bookmarks yet. Add one, or bring them from your browser.
bookmarks.emptyFav: No favourites yet. Mark one with the star in its menu.
bookmarks.importLead: A bookmarks file exported from Chrome, Firefox, Safari or Edge (.html), or a backup of this app (.json).
bookmarks.importAdd: Add them in a new folder
bookmarks.importNone: No bookmarks found in that file.
bookmarks.replaceQ: Your {have} bookmarks will be replaced by the {n} in the file.
bookmarks.cannotOpen: This address cannot be opened from here.
bookmarks.notLoaded: Your bookmarks could not be read yet. Tap the sync status to try again.
bookmarks.merged: Merged with the changes made on another device.
bookmarks.bookmarkletLead: Drag this button to your browser's bookmarks bar. Then, on any web page, click it: Bookmarks opens with that page ready to save.
bookmarks.exportLead: The .html file opens in Chrome, Firefox, Safari and Edge. The .json keeps tags, notes and favourites for this app.
bookmarks.dupesLead: The same address saved more than once. The marked copy stays and gets the others' tags, notes and star.
bookmarks.introLead: Your web links in folders. Tap a card to open the link; long-press or right-click it for more. Drag cards onto folders to move them.
bookmarks.introSearch: Search titles, addresses, tags and notes (Ctrl+/). Type #tag to search tags only.
bookmarks.introMore: Import, export, find duplicates, sort and select.
bookmarks.introList: Show bookmarks as a compact list.
bookmarks.introSync: Green when everything is saved. Tap it to refresh.
